profile.headline: Software Engineer | Nation Builder 27 & ReReads | ex-Microsoft | React, TypeScript, Accessibility
profile.summary:
I'm a software engineer with nine years of experience building things people actually use.
 
Seven of those were at Microsoft on the End User Engineering team, where I built shared React Native components used across an employee app and its partner teams, made a dashboard work properly for people navigating by screen reader, and served as the primary UI engineer on the internal portal that kept thousands of conference rooms running.
 
Right now I'm the founding engineer at Circa Games, building Nation Builder 27 in Electron, React and TypeScript. I own the entire technical stack. That means a deterministic turn engine resolving fourteen interdependent systems across a 900-turn campaign, a versioned save format with schema migration so content updates never corrupt existing saves, and a data pipeline driving 161 playable nations. It's the most complete piece of engineering I've been responsible for start to finish.
 
I also built and run ReReads, a spoiler-free recap site for book series, and I work part-time at an independent bookstore in Pioneer Square.
 
Teaching runs through most of my career. I taught JavaScript workshops at General Assembly, built curriculum at Justice Reskill for students moving into tech from justice involvement, mentored at Year Up, and served on the board of Womxn of Color in Tech. At Microsoft I hosted and produced live sessions for Career Week and moderated panels. Explaining hard things clearly is the part of this work I like most.
 
I'm looking for front-end or full-stack engineering work where I can own real surface area. If you're building something complicated, say hi.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Nation Builder 27 

- Sole engineer on a cross-platform desktop strategy game built in Electron, React, and TypeScript. A design partner authors all narrative content and a balanced design; I build the software.
  
- Architected a deterministic turn engine that resolves 14 interdependent systems (economy, population, governance, elections, trade, military, nations) in predictable order with no hidden state, across a 900-turn campaign covering 161 real nations.
 
- Refactored a monolithic React app into modular pure-function simulation modules separated from view logic, behind a centralized TypeScript type layer. Built a versioned save/load system with schema migration so content updates never corrupt existing saves, plus a JSON data pipeline driving era and tier gating across 41 buildings, 30 industries, and 80 commodities.

positions.title: Full Stack Developer at Microsoft
positions.description:
I designed, built, and managed the consumer facing site for the Interoperability Events Team. The site was seen and used across the world. I redesigned the site to follow Microsoft brand standards, which helped increase site views and event attendance. I also made updates to the admin portal of the site and how users logged into the site. The site was built with Node.js, Angular.js, Bootstrap, and HTML/CSS.

https://interopevents.com/

I also, built demos for the team that were used in events around the world. One of the demos I built was used in an Outlook extension.

positions.title: Full Stack Engineer
positions.description: Responsible for maintaining and adding new features to consumer-facing event websites for interoperability events. Created, implemented, and performed user testing on a new UI design for the website. Ensured the site was responsive and accessible. Rebuilt the site's admin portal and user authentication flow. Gathered requirements from stakeholders and built event demos, one of which was adopted into an Outlook extension.

projects.title: Listo
projects.description: This is a social media app that is designed to group 4 members together based on their neighborhood and uses foursquare's api to select a random location for a meet up. What makes Listo unique is its flake score which allows users to see how flakey each user is. This ensures that users show up to events.
